purpose: A reference .NET application implementing an e-commerce website using microservices architecture
description: eShop is a .NET Aspire-based reference application showcasing a services-based e-commerce platform. It demonstrates microservices patterns with Catalog, Basket, Ordering, Identity, and Webhook APIs, uses PostgreSQL with pgvector for data storage, RabbitMQ for event-driven communication, and Redis for caching. The application includes a Blazor-based WebApp, MAUI mobile client support, and integrates OpenTelemetry for observability.

prerequisites: Visual Studio 2022 v17.10+ with ASP.NET workload and .NET Aspire SDK (Windows), OR
Optional: Visual Studio Code with C# Dev Kit
Optional: .NET MAUI workload for mobile client
steps: Open eShop.Web.slnf in Visual Studio and set eShop.AppHost as startup project, OR run from terminal
Press Ctrl-F5 in VS or execute the dotnet run command
Open the Aspire dashboard URL shown in console output (http://localhost:19888/login?t=...)
Access the eShop web application through the Aspire dashboard

commonErrors.fix: Start Docker Desktop and ensure it's fully running before launching the application

commonErrors.error: Port conflicts on 19888 or other ports
commonErrors.fix: Stop other services using those ports or restart Docker Desktop
Run 'dotnet dev-certs https --trust' and close all browser tabs

entrypoints.description: Aspire app host that orchestrates all microservices, databases, and message brokers

workflows.name: Playwright E2E Tests
mainSteps: Run Playwright tests for web UI

howToAddFeature: Review CONTRIBUTING.md for principles: best practices, architectural integrity, realistic tech choices
For new microservice: Create service project in src/, add to eShop.AppHost/Program.cs orchestration
For API changes: Follow minimal API pattern in existing services, use versioned endpoints
Add integration events in EventBus if service-to-service communication needed
Update AppHost to wire dependencies (databases, message queues, service references)
Add corresponding unit/integration tests in tests/ directory
Consider adding Playwright e2e tests in e2e/ if UI is affected
howToAddTest: Unit tests: Create/add to tests/{ServiceName}.UnitTests project
Integration tests: Use WebApplicationFactory and TestHost for API testing
E2E tests: Add .spec.ts files in e2e/ directory using Playwright
Run tests with 'dotnet test' or 'npx playwright test'
contrib.codeStyle: Follow .NET best practices and canonical patterns. Use minimal APIs with extension methods for service registration and endpoint mapping. Apply central package management via Directory.Packages.props. Use structured logging, health checks, and OpenTelemetry. See .editorconfig for formatting rules.

architecture.overview: eShop uses a microservices architecture orchestrated by .NET Aspire. Each service is independently deployable with its own database. Services communicate via RabbitMQ event bus for async operations and gRPC for sync calls. The Aspire AppHost manages service discovery, configuration, and observability. Frontend uses Blazor for web and .NET MAUI for mobile clients.

components.name: Catalog.API
components.description: Manages product catalog with PostgreSQL + pgvector for AI-enhanced search. Publishes integration events for catalog changes.

components.name: Basket.API
components.description: Shopping basket service using Redis for fast storage. Exposes gRPC endpoints and subscribes to order events.

components.name: Ordering.API
components.description: Order processing with DDD patterns (domain models, aggregates). Uses PostgreSQL and publishes order lifecycle events.

components.name: Identity.API
components.description: Authentication/authorization using Duende IdentityServer with JWT tokens.

components.name: Webhooks.API
components.description: Manages webhook subscriptions and delivery for external integrations.

components.name: WebApp
components.description: Blazor Server web UI consuming backend APIs with service discovery.

components.name: OrderProcessor & PaymentProcessor
components.description: Background workers processing orders and payments via event bus.

components.name: EventBus
components.description: Abstraction layer for pub/sub messaging with RabbitMQ implementation.

components.name: ServiceDefaults
components.description: Shared extensions for observability, health checks, resilience, and service discovery.

architecture.dataFlow: User interacts with WebApp (Blazor) → WebApp calls backend APIs via HTTP → APIs use service discovery to locate each other → Async operations publish events to RabbitMQ → Background workers/services subscribe and react → Each service maintains its own database (Catalog, Order, Identity in PostgreSQL; Basket in Redis) → All telemetry flows to Aspire dashboard via OpenTelemetry

keyAbstractions.name: IEventBus
keyAbstractions.description: Abstraction for publishing and subscribing to integration events across microservices. Implemented by RabbitMQ.

keyAbstractions.name: IntegrationEvent
keyAbstractions.description: Base class for events that cross service boundaries. Includes correlation and timestamp metadata.

keyAbstractions.name: ServiceDefaults extensions
keyAbstractions.description: Extension methods (AddServiceDefaults, MapDefaultEndpoints) that configure health checks, telemetry, resilience, and service discovery for all services.

keyAbstractions.name: Minimal API with versioning
keyAbstractions.description: Endpoints defined via MapGroup with explicit API versions (v1, v2) for backward compatibility.

keyAbstractions.name: Aspire ResourceBuilder
keyAbstractions.description: Fluent API in AppHost for configuring services, databases, message brokers, and their dependencies.

codeExamples.title: Minimal API endpoint with versioning
codeExamples.explanation: Shows how eShop uses minimal APIs with explicit versioning, descriptive metadata, and route grouping for clean API design.

codeExamples.title: Service defaults registration
codeExamples.explanation: Every service follows this pattern: AddServiceDefaults() configures observability, health checks, and resilience; AddApplicationServices() registers service-specific dependencies.

codeExamples.title: Aspire service orchestration
codeExamples.explanation: Aspire AppHost declaratively configures infrastructure (Redis, RabbitMQ, Postgres) and services with dependencies, ensuring proper startup order.

codeExamples.title: Publishing integration event
codeExamples.explanation: Integration events inherit from IntegrationEvent base class and are published via IEventBus. Subscribers in other services react to these events asynchronously.

firstTasks.title: Add product filtering by price range
firstTasks.description: Extend the Catalog API to accept min/max price query parameters and filter results. Update the CatalogApi.cs GetAllItems endpoint.
firstTasks.why: Great first feature that introduces you to minimal APIs, query parameter binding, and EF Core queries without touching complex business logic.

firstTasks.title: Add unit tests for BasketService gRPC endpoints
firstTasks.description: Create comprehensive tests for the basket gRPC service methods (GetBasket, UpdateBasket, DeleteBasket) using NSubstitute mocks.
firstTasks.why: Familiarizes you with the testing patterns, MSTest framework, and gRPC service implementation while improving test coverage.

firstTasks.title: Improve error messages in CONTRIBUTING.md
firstTasks.description: Expand the contribution guide with common development pitfalls (Docker not running, certificate trust issues, port conflicts) and their solutions.
firstTasks.why: Low barrier to entry, helps you understand the developer experience, and makes a real impact for future contributors.

firstTasks.title: Add Playwright test for order placement flow
firstTasks.description: Create an e2e test that adds items to basket, proceeds to checkout, and verifies order confirmation. Follow patterns in existing test files.
firstTasks.why: Introduces you to the full user flow, Playwright testing patterns, and how services interact end-to-end.

firstTasks.title: Implement caching for catalog item queries
firstTasks.description: Add Redis caching to frequently accessed catalog endpoints. Use IDistributedCache and implement cache invalidation when items are updated.
firstTasks.why: Teaches performance optimization patterns, distributed caching with Redis, and introduces you to Aspire's Redis integration.

firstTasks.title: Refactor OrderingAPI to use MediatR pipeline behaviors
firstTasks.description: Extract cross-cutting concerns (logging, validation) into MediatR pipeline behaviors to reduce duplication in command handlers.
firstTasks.why: Demonstrates CQRS and MediatR patterns while improving code quality. Shows how to work with the domain-driven design structure.

firstTasks.title: Add health check for external AI service connectivity
firstTasks.description: Implement custom IHealthCheck for Azure OpenAI connection status and integrate with existing health check infrastructure.
firstTasks.why: Dives into observability patterns, custom health checks, and integration with Aspire dashboard. Critical for production readiness.

firstTasks.title: Implement saga pattern for order cancellation
firstTasks.description: Create a distributed transaction saga to handle order cancellation across Ordering, Basket, and Payment services using compensating events.
firstTasks.why: Tackles complex distributed systems challenges, event-driven architecture, and eventual consistency. Showcases real-world microservices patterns.

deploySteps: Ensure Azure subscription is active and Azure Developer CLI (azd) is installed
Execute 'azd init' from repository root and select .NET Aspire project
Choose services to expose publicly (typically WebApp)
Run 'azd up' to provision Azure resources and deploy
Access the application via the URL provided by azd output
For updates, run 'azd up' again after code changes
observability: Aspire Dashboard: Local development access at http://localhost:19888 to view logs, traces, and metrics for all services
OpenTelemetry: All services emit telemetry (logs, traces, metrics) via OpenTelemetry configured in ServiceDefaults
Health Checks: Each service exposes /health and /alive endpoints viewable via Aspire dashboard or direct HTTP calls
Structured Logging: Services use ILogger with structured logging, aggregated logs visible in Aspire dashboard

incidents.name: Service not starting
incidents.check: Check Aspire dashboard for service status. Verify Docker containers are running. Check dependency health (Postgres, Redis, RabbitMQ). Review service logs for startup errors.

incidents.name: Database connection failures
incidents.check: Verify Postgres container is healthy. Check connection strings in Aspire configuration. Ensure EF migrations have run (OrderingAPI should run first).

incidents.name: Event bus messages not flowing
incidents.check: Verify RabbitMQ container is running. Check RabbitMQ management UI (if exposed). Review service logs for subscription errors. Ensure event handlers are registered.

incidents.name: Authentication failures
incidents.check: Verify Identity.API is running and healthy. Check JWT token configuration. Ensure Identity database is seeded. Review CORS settings if calling from browser.

incidents.name: High latency or timeouts
incidents.check: Check Aspire dashboard for slow traces. Review database query performance. Check Redis connectivity. Verify resilience policies (retry, circuit breaker) in ServiceDefaults.
